Figure 1:Detection AUC against embedding wall-clock time for each optimization
strategy. Restricting backpropagation to the last four transformer blocks gives
the best balance of embedding quality and speed.

Figure 2:Probability that a randomly selected insecure-code example receives a higher gradient-similarity score than a randomly selected secure-code example (ROC-AUC), before and after insecure-code fine-tuning. This measures score ordering, not the frequency of harmful responses.
Figure 3:SafeTulu construction: score Tulu 3 examples against unsafe SafeRLHF responses, remove the 20% with the highest gradient similarity, and train and evaluate on the retained 80%.

Figure 4:Evaluation results after baseline training, training on randomly filtered data, training on the LLM-as-a-judge filtered dataset, training on data filtered with the method of He et al., and training on SafeTulu. All values are percentages, reported as mean±\pmstandard error. Lower is better on GCG & ActorBreaker attack success rate and ORBench over-refusal rate, while higher accuracy is better on all capability metrics. Across all models, training on SafeTulu decreases ASR while preserving comparable capability.
